moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Preparing Android Devices, Emulators & Simulators
learningObjectives: Prepare a physical Android device for automation: USB debugging, drivers, and phone-data access.
Create and use an Android emulator through Android Studio's AVD Manager.
Diagnose vendor-specific Android restrictions using the device and Agent documentation.
Retrieve the AppPackage and AppActivity values Tosca needs to open an installed Android app.

elements.title: Android prerequisites
items: On the device, allow access to phone data when prompted.

Enable USB debugging: Settings → Developer options → USB debugging (Developer options itself is usually hidden — enable it first by tapping the Build number field, under Settings → About phone, seven times).
Ensure the correct USB driver for that device is installed on the computer running TMA.
Unlock the device and authorize the computer’s RSA debugging key when prompted. Trust can need renewal after authorizations are revoked or the host key changes.

elements.text: Charging or file-transfer visibility alone does not establish debugging access. Check USB debugging authorization and adb devices before investigating the Agent connection.

bulletPoints: Allow phone data access · enable USB debugging · install the USB driver · accept the on-device debugging prompt.

elements.term: Android Studio and the AVD Manager
elements.description: Tricentis recommends Android Studio for emulators. Its AVD (Android Virtual Device) Manager creates emulator profiles by pairing a device definition (e.g. Pixel 7) with a system image (a specific Android version and CPU architecture).

elements.title: Creating an AVD
items: Check the current Android Studio host requirements and install a compatible system image through SDK Manager.
In Device Manager, choose Create Device and select a hardware profile.
Select a compatible system image, review the AVD configuration, and finish.
Start the emulator, wait for Android to become usable, and verify Agent detection. An adb device entry alone does not prove that boot has completed.

elements.text: For the documented TMA 2025.4 setup, run the emulator on the Agent host. This supported topology is not a claim that every remote Android connection is technically impossible.

bulletPoints: AVD = device definition + system image, created and run through Android Studio.
Use the documented Agent-host emulator topology and verify readiness separately from detection.

elements.text: Google’s Android Studio Windows requirements checked on 2026-10-06 do not support ARM-based Windows CPUs. Choose a supported host for this setup or investigate a supported physical-device configuration; re-check the published matrix when versions change.

elements.title: Device-side gotchas that look like Tosca problems
items: Samsung Auto Blocker can block USB commands when enabled. Check the model, software version and approved test-device security configuration rather than assuming one setting or default applies to all Galaxy devices.

TMA 2025.4 troubleshooting does discuss Permission Monitoring, including Xiaomi/Oppo restrictions. Settings vary by vendor and build; an absent toggle is not proof of readiness or a reason to bypass applicable device policy.

For an APK certificate error, preserve the exact error and verify the supplied APK with apksigner verify. Ask the application owner for a correctly signed, compatible test build instead of assuming every error is caused by a v1-only signature or automatically replacing its signing key.

bulletPoints: Check host support against the current published requirements.
Diagnose vendor restrictions and APK signing separately; avoid universal fixes based only on a symptom.

elements.description: For an installed Android application, specify its package and intended launch activity in AppPackage and AppActivity. Obtain these from the application owner or verified build configuration; a focused activity is not necessarily its launch entry point.

elements.title: Verify the launch configuration
items: Obtain the package identifier and launch activity for the exact test build.
Confirm that the target application is installed on the selected device.
Use AppPackage and AppActivity with ActionMode Input and verify that the intended application opens.

elements.text: adb belongs to SDK Platform Tools. Use SDK Manager to install that package or check the Agent’s documented platform-tools directory for the executable; do not assume that every Android Studio installation already has it.

Application Path can install an Android APK. BundleID identifies an installed iOS application. Prefer AppPackage/AppActivity for the installed Android application rather than treating all other fields as APK-installation fields.

bulletPoints: Use verified Android package and launch activity values for an installed app.
Check that the SDK Platform Tools or Agent adb executable is available.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a charging, OS-visible device is automation-ready
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Connecting a phone by USB, seeing it recognised by the operating system, and concluding it's ready for TMA.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: USB debugging must be explicitly enabled under Developer options, phone data access allowed, and the correct USB driver installed. A device can be fully visible to the OS while still refusing debugging access.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming one Samsung security configuration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for the USB debugging toggle on a recent Samsung device and finding it greyed out or missing.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check whether Auto Blocker is enabled and whether it blocks USB commands on the particular model and software version. Follow the approved test-device configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to create an Android emulator on Windows on ARM
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing Android Studio on an ARM64 Windows machine and hunting for the missing emulator SDK package.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The published Windows requirements currently exclude ARM-based CPUs. Check host compatibility before reinstalling tools; use a supported setup and re-check future requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Installing an old training APK on a new Android version
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Getting INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_NO_CERTIFICATES when installing an APK that used to work fine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify the APK signature and supported platform range with apksigner, retain the installation error, and request a compatible signed build from the application owner. Do not infer the signature scheme or replace the signing key from the error name alone.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which three settings does the documented TMA physical Android preparation cover? (three correct answers)

options.text: USB debugging enabled under Developer options
Phone data access allowed on the device
The correct USB driver installed on the TMA machine

practiceQuiz.hint: A particular charge percentage is not a debugging setting.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The preparation covers debugging, data access and host drivers. Sufficient power is needed to operate the phone, but a 100% battery is not a required setting.

optionExplanations.A: USB debugging enables the documented USB automation connection.
optionExplanations.B: Allowing phone-data access is part of the documented device preparation.
optionExplanations.C: Install the applicable host USB driver as documented for the device.
optionExplanations.D: The phone needs enough power to operate, not a specific 100% charge.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Samsung test phone has Auto Blocker enabled and USB commands are blocked. Which feature should the team investigate under its approved device policy?

options.text: The phone needs a factory reset.
The enabled Auto Blocker security feature.
USB debugging was removed from Android entirely.
TMA must be running before the toggle becomes available.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the confirmed setting in the scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Samsung documents USB-command blocking by Auto Blocker when enabled. Available settings vary by model and software; this is not a universal diagnosis for every greyed-out debugging toggle.

optionExplanations.A: No evidence in this scenario requires erasing the device.
optionExplanations.B: The confirmed enabled feature can block USB commands.
optionExplanations.C: Android still supports USB debugging; a vendor restriction is different.
optionExplanations.D: Starting TMA does not override this phone security setting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Android Studio Windows requirements checked for this lesson exclude ARM-based CPUs. Why should a learner verify host support before diagnosing AVD setup on an ARM64 Windows laptop?

options.text: The SDK Manager needs to be reinstalled.
The host falls outside the published Windows CPU support requirements for this setup.
The learner needs a paid Android Studio licence.
TMA must be installed before the emulator package appears.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a supported host from a reinstall or licence issue.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The checked Windows support matrix excludes ARM-based CPUs. Use a supported configuration and consult updated requirements when versions change; this is not a permanent statement about all future emulator packages.

optionExplanations.A: Reinstalling does not change the host CPU support matrix.
optionExplanations.B: The host is outside the checked Windows requirements.
optionExplanations.C: A paid licence is not the missing host-support requirement.
optionExplanations.D: Installing TMA does not add Android Studio host support.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Open Mobile App fields specify the package and launch activity of an already-installed Android app?

options.text: Application Path to an APK only

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the Android application, not the iOS app or the connection.
practiceQuiz.rationale: AppPackage and AppActivity identify the installed Android application to open. Application Path instead supplies an APK to install; BundleID is the installed iOS identifier.

optionExplanations.A: BundleID is used for installed iOS apps.
optionExplanations.B: These are the documented installed Android application identifiers.
optionExplanations.C: Application Path supplies an APK for installation rather than these identifiers.
optionExplanations.D: These configure the device/server connection, not the target application.

quickRecap.value: Authorize USB debugging, allow data access and check the applicable host driver.
Create an AVD from a hardware profile and compatible system image; verify boot readiness and Agent detection.
When enabled, Auto Blocker can block USB commands; inspect the actual model and approved settings.
TMA troubleshooting includes vendor-specific permission restrictions. Check the actual device build.
Verify the supplied APK signature and request a compatible signed test build; do not automatically re-sign it.
The checked Android Studio Windows CPU matrix excludes ARM hosts; re-check version support.
Use verified AppPackage/AppActivity for installed Android apps; BundleID is for iOS.
adb is part of SDK Platform Tools; verify that the SDK or Agent executable is installed.

platformVersion: TMA 2025.4 / Tosca 2026.1 LTS; Android documentation checked 2026-10-06
